title: February Revolution
summary: Bread queues and a strike in Petrograd at the end of February 1917 became a revolution in a week when the garrison refused to fire and then joined the crowds; Nicholas II abdicated on 15 March and his brother declined the throne the next day. Power passed to a Provisional Government drawn from the Duma and, beside it, to the Petrograd Soviet of workers' and soldiers' deputies — the dual power that governed Russia until October. It is in the atlas as the end of three centuries of Romanov rule and as the eight months in which the question was not whether Russia would be a republic but which republic it would be.
